items.title: Section: Non-Analytical Cessation — When Something Fails to Arise Simply Because Its Rival Already Has

items.zh: 復次，云何非擇滅？謂若餘法生緣現前，餘法生故，餘不得生，唯滅、唯靜，名非擇滅。諸所有法此時應生，越生時故，彼於此時終不更生。
items.en:
Second, non-analytical cessation; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is non-analytical cessation?
Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment; first, stating its name. Whenever the conditions for one phenomenon's arising are present and it arises, some other phenomenon is thereby prevented from arising — this simple cessation and stillness is called non-analytical cessation.
Second, explaining its characteristic. Whatever should have arisen at a given moment, once that moment for arising has passed, will never arise at that time again.

items.title: Section: The Hundred-Forbearances Elder — And Why a Stream-Enterer's Own Non-Arising Is Absolutely Final

items.zh: 是故此滅亦是假有，非實物有。所以者何？此無有餘自相可得故。此法種類非離繫故，復於餘時遇緣可生。是故非擇滅非一向決定。若學見跡，於卵、濕二生，北拘盧洲、無想天、若女、若扇搋迦、若半擇迦、無形、二形等生，及於後有若愛、若願所得非擇滅，當知一向決定。由學見迹、甞不於後有起希願纏，發生後有，唯除未無餘永害愛種子故。
items.en:
Second, distinguishing whether it is provisional or real; first, stating it is provisional. Therefore this cessation, too, is merely provisionally existent, not any substantially real entity. Second, explaining why. Why is this so? Because it has no further distinguishing characteristic of its own.
Third, distinguishing its kinds; first, not absolutely final. Since this kind of phenomenon is not free of its underlying bond, it may still arise again at another time given the right conditions — non-analytical cessation is therefore not absolutely final.
Second, absolutely final; first, stating the category. A learner who has seen the noble truths directly will never again be born from an egg or from moisture, in Uttarakuru or the heaven of no-thought, as a woman, lacking male capacity in any form, and the non-analytical cessation obtained with respect to craving or aspiration towards a future rebirth should be known as absolutely final.
Second, explaining why. Because a learner who has seen the noble truths directly never again gives rise to the entanglement of craving or aspiration towards a future rebirth such as would bring that rebirth about, except for the seed of craving not yet entirely eradicated.

items.title: Section: Six Kinds of Skilful Understanding Overview — And the Six-Angle Analysis of the Aggregates Begins

items.zh: 問：何因緣故，名心不相應耶？答：此是假想，於諸事中為起言說，於有色等二種俱非，於有見等二種俱非。如是廣說安立道理，一切當知。如是已說六種善巧，謂蘊善巧乃至根善巧，云何應知是諸善巧廣建立義？復次，嗢柁南曰：自性、義、差別、次第、攝、依止。
items.en:
Second, explaining the name "mind-dissociated"; first, the question. Question: for what reason are these called mind-dissociated? Second, the answer. Answer: these are mere conceptual designations, established within various matters for the sake of verbal expression, being neither form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible.
Second, the conclusion. One should know all of this has now been explained in full regarding the principle of their provisional establishment.
Fifth, the six kinds of skilful understanding; first, referring back and introducing what follows. Having thus named the six kinds of skilful understanding — the aggregates and so on through the faculties — how should one understand the extensive meaning of their establishment?
Second, explaining each individually; first, the extensive establishment; first, skilful understanding of the aggregates; first, generally distinguishing six aspects; first, a summarising verse. Furthermore, the summarising verse states: essential nature, meaning, distinctions, sequence, subsumption, and support.

items.title: Section: What Is Form, Fundamentally? Eleven Kinds Reducing to Two, All Sharing One Common Mark

items.zh: 問：何等是色自性？答：略有十一。謂眼等十色處及法處所攝色。又總有二，謂四大種及所造色。如是一切皆變礙相。
items.en:
Second, the prose explanation; first, essential nature; first, the explanation; first, form; first, the question. Question: what is form's own essential nature?
Second, the answer; first, its self-characteristic nature; first, eleven kinds. Answer: in brief, there are eleven — the ten sense-bases of form beginning with the eye, together with form subsumed under the sense-base of mental objects.
Second, two kinds. Altogether, there are also two: the four great elements, and derived form.
Second, its shared characteristic nature. All of these alike bear the mark of mutability and obstruction.

items.title: Section: The Subtlest Form of All — Generated by Concentration Rather Than the Elements Directly — and Feeling's Six-Then-Two-Fold Nature

items.zh: 問：何等是受自性？答：略有六種。謂依眼等六觸所生。此復二種，若色為依名身受，無色為依名心受。何以故？由前五根皆色性故。
items.en:
Second, feeling; first, the question. Question: what is feeling's own essential nature?
Second, the answer; first, its self-characteristic nature; first, six kinds. Answer: in brief, there are six — feeling arising through contact via the eye and the rest.
Second, two kinds; first, stating the distinction. This is further of two kinds: feeling dependent on form is called bodily feeling; feeling dependent on the formless is called mental feeling. Second, explaining accordingly. Why is this so? Because the first five sense-faculties are all material in nature.

items.title: Section: Why the Five Senses Share One Name, "Body," While the Mind Stands Entirely Apart

items.zh: 問：若前五根皆是色性，依眼等受名身受者，何故眼等非唯是身？答：由相異故。所以者何？眼等五根展轉相異。問：若眼等根其相異故，非皆身相，依彼諸受，由是因緣應非身受？答：餘有色根不離身故。就彼為名，此復何過。問：若不離身故無過者，意根亦爾，不離身轉，依意根受應名身受。是即一切皆是身受，無心受耶？答：諸有色根定不離身，意即不爾，故無有過。所以者何？生無色界有情，意根離身而轉。是故五根所生諸受合名身受，唯依意者獨名心受。故總說二，謂身、心受。
items.en:
Third, a question-and-answer analysis; first, regarding the five sense-faculties; first, the question. Question: if the first five faculties are all material, and feeling arising through them is called bodily feeling, why are these five not simply called "body" themselves? Second, the answer. Answer: because their characteristics differ from one another; the five sense-faculties mutually differ in this way.
Second, regarding bodily feeling; first, the question. Question: if the five sense-faculties differ in characteristic and are not simply "the body" itself, should feeling dependent on them, for this same reason, not be called bodily feeling? Second, the answer. Answer: since these material faculties are never apart from the body, naming their feeling accordingly involves no fault.
Third, regarding the mental faculty; first, the question. Question: if being inseparable from the body avoids fault, the mental faculty is likewise never apart from the body — should feeling dependent on it not then also be called bodily feeling, making all feeling bodily feeling with no mental feeling at all?
Second, the answer; first, distinguishing the two. Answer: the material faculties are necessarily inseparable from the body; the mental faculty is not — therefore no fault follows. Second, explaining why. Why is this so? Because beings reborn in the formless realm have a mental faculty functioning apart from the body.
Fourth, establishing the account. Therefore feeling arising through the five sense-faculties is collectively called bodily feeling, while feeling dependent on the mental faculty alone is uniquely called mental feeling — hence the two are together called bodily and mental feeling.

items.title: Section: "I Accept No View" — The Paradox That Made Śāriputra an Arhat on the Spot

items.en: Second, its shared characteristic nature. Every feeling, without exception, bears the mark of reception.

items.zh: 問：何等是想自性？答：此亦六種，如前應知。又想有六。

items.title: Section: Narrow, Vast, Immeasurable, and Empty Perception — And the Novice's Oil-Smeared Bowl That Neither Has Nor Lacks Oil

items.zh: 一、有相想，二、無相想，三、狹小想，四、廣大想，五、無量想，六、無所有想。又略有二。一、世間想，二、出世想。狹小想者，謂欲廛想。廣大想者，謂色廛想。無量想者，謂空、識無邊處廛想。無所有想者，謂無所有處廛想。即此一切名有相想。無相想者，謂有頂想及一切出世間學無學想。
items.en:
First, narrow perception. Narrow perception is perception bound by the desire realm. Second, vast perception. Vast perception is perception bound by the form realm.
Third, immeasurable perception. Immeasurable perception is perception bound by the spheres of infinite space and infinite consciousness. Fourth, nothing-at-all perception. Nothing-at-all perception is perception bound by the sphere of nothingness.
Fifth, marked perception. All of the above together are called marked perception. Sixth, unmarked perception. Unmarked perception is the perception of the summit of existence, together with every transmundane perception of those in training and beyond training.

items.title: Section: Perception's Single Shared Mark — And Mental Formations Begin With Five Functions of the Restless Will

items.zh: 又一切想皆等了相。問：何等是行自性？答：此亦六種。如前應知。又此行相，由五種類令心造作。一、為境隨與，二、為彼合會，三、為彼別離，四、能發雜染業，五、令心自在轉。
items.en:
Second, its shared characteristic nature. Every perception, without exception, bears the mark of equally apprehending its object.
Fourth, formations; first, the question. Question: what is formations' own essential nature? Second, the answer; first, its self-characteristic nature; first, six kinds. Answer: this too is of six kinds, as already explained before.
Second, five kinds. Formations, considered by how they cause the mind to act, are of five kinds: first, going along with the object; second, uniting with it; third, separating from it; fourth, generating defiled karma; fifth, enabling the mind to turn freely.

items.title: Section: Formations Complete With Their Shared Mark of Construction — And Consciousness, the Fifth Aggregate, Begins

items.zh: 又此行相略有三種。一者、善行，二、不善行，三、無記行。又一切行皆造作相。
items.en:
Third, three kinds. Formations, in brief, are further of three kinds: first, wholesome formations; second, unwholesome formations; third, neutral formations.
Second, their shared characteristic nature. All formations, without exception, bear the mark of active construction.
Fifth, consciousness; first, the question.

items.title: Section: Consciousness's Eighteen Self-Natures Complete the Aggregates' Essential Nature in Full

items.zh: 問：何等是識自性？答：略有六種。所謂眼識乃至意識，是識自性差別。又識有三種。一、領受差別，二、採境差別，三、分位差別。領受差別有三，採境差別有六，分位差別有三。如是識蘊差別，總有十八自性應知。是名諸蘊自性。
items.en:
Fifth, consciousness; first, the question. Question: what is consciousness's own essential nature? Second, the answer; first, stating and listing; first, six kinds. Answer: in brief, there are six — eye-consciousness through mental consciousness, each a distinct self-nature of consciousness.
Second, three kinds; first, briefly. Consciousness is further of three kinds: distinction by reception, by object-apprehension, and by temporal stage. Second, in detail. Distinction by reception is threefold, by object-apprehension sixfold, and by temporal stage threefold.
Second, the overall conclusion. Thus consciousness's distinctions total eighteen self-natures, one should know. Second, the conclusion. This is called the essential nature of the aggregates.

items.title: Section: What "Aggregate" Actually Means — Eleven Angles Applied to Every One of the Five

items.zh: 復次，蘊義云何？為顯何義，建立諸蘊？謂所有色，若去來今乃至遠近。如色，乃至識亦爾。如是總略攝一切蘊，積聚義是蘊義。
items.en:
Second, their meaning; first, the two questions posed together. Furthermore, what is the meaning of "aggregate"? And to reveal what truth were the aggregates established?
Second, answering separately; first, answering the meaning of "aggregate"; first, the meaning of distinction; first, taking up form. All form whatsoever — whether past, future, present, and so on through far and near.
Second, extending this to the rest. As with form, so too with feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness.
Second, the overall summary meaning. Gathering together all of this under one summary term across every aggregate — this accumulated gathering is precisely the meaning of "aggregate."

blocks.text: Two more unconditioned things, and then a fresh pass over the five aggregates: what each one fundamentally is.

When the conditions for one thing are present and it arises, another is kept from arising; this simple non-arising is "non-analytical cessation". Master Cháng Bǎi: "other" means opposed things, like pain and pleasure, light and dark.

Such a thing is not free of its bond and can arise later. Master Cháng Bǎi: an affliction not yet severed, absent only for lack of conditions, is this kind of cessation. A stream-enterer no longer moistens rebirth with conceptually acquired craving.
They are "established within various matters for verbal expression, neither form nor formless".
Eleven kinds; in sum, two (the elements and derived form); its shared mark, mutability and obstruction.
Feeling dependent on form is bodily feeling; on the formless, mental feeling. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodily feeling is feeling joined with the five sense consciousnesses.
Master Cháng Bǎi: formless beings have no coarse form, and the mental faculty functions alone.
Unmarked perception is that of the summit of existence and every transmundane perception; all before it is "marked". (Untranslated, 0593b27: "What is the nature of perception? Six kinds, as before.")

Yielding to the object, uniting with it, separating from it, generating defiled karma, and enabling the mind to turn freely. Master Cháng Bǎi: volition follows along and moves the mind towards or away from objects.
Six consciousnesses, plus three further distinctions, for eighteen. Its shared mark, discernment, "is easy to understand, and so it is left unsaid".
Each aggregate gathers its kinds, past, future, present, near and far; this gathering is the meaning of "aggregate". The aggregates are nothing but conditioned things under various names.
"Aggregate" means heap. The teaching invites us to see the self as five heaps, not one thing.

options: when conditions for one phenomenon arise, another cannot arise; simple stillness, and past its moment it does not arise at that time
a cessation by wisdom's discrimination that severs afflictions forever
the temporary stopping of mind and factors in the attainment of cessation
the impermanence of phenomena perishing of themselves after arising
quiz.why: The treatise says that when the conditions for one phenomenon are present and it arises, another is thereby kept from arising, and this simple cessation and stillness is non-analytical cessation; whatever should have arisen at that moment will not arise at that time. Master Cháng Bǎi: a phenomenon's not appearing here is not the result of wisdom's discrimination, which is what distinguishes it from analytical cessation.

quiz.q: The English has "some other, mutually exclusive phenomenon." What is the source and range of this addition?
options: it comes from the Sub-commentary's opposed phenomena, like light and dark; but the lecturer also gives mere lack of conditions, so it is narrower
it is literal: 餘 itself means opposed, so the English is word for word
it comes from the Sarvāstivāda definition of analytical cessation and should be deleted
it comes from the lecturer's Xuánzàng story and has nothing to do with the Sub-commentary
quiz.why: The Chinese has only 餘, "other." The Sub-commentary glosses it as mutually opposed phenomena such as pain and pleasure or light and dark, and Master Cháng Bǎi follows: phenomena of opposed nature, regarding one another, are called "other." Yet his own example is a person who simply has no occasion to speak. So "mutually exclusive" is the Sub-commentary's reading, written into the translation.

quiz.q: When is non-analytical cessation not absolutely final, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: when an affliction is already severed for good, yet it appears again when the conditions are complete
in the attainment of cessation, after which nothing appears again
when an affliction is not severed and simply lacks conditions, so that it will appear when conditions meet
on rebirth in the heaven of no-thought, after which it never arises
quiz.why: The treatise explains that such a phenomenon is not free of its bond and can arise at another time given conditions. Master Cháng Bǎi: if an affliction has not been severed and does not appear only for lack of conditions, this is non-analytical cessation, and it is not final, for it appears again when conditions are complete. An absence of anger, for example, does not prove anger is gone.

quiz.q: The English has "never again gives rise to craving or aspiration towards a future rebirth." What key point is left out?
options: 纏 and 發生後有 are omitted: what is cut is conceptually acquired craving; craving seeds remain, and a stream-enterer still has up to seven lives
希願 is omitted: a stream-enterer still longs for rebirth but does not voice it
學見跡 is omitted: the passage concerns arhats, not stream-enterers
nothing is omitted: a stream-enterer is never reborn again, so the English is exact
quiz.why: The Chinese speaks of the wrapping of aspiration, 希願纏, which brings about a future existence. Master Cháng Bǎi: a stream-enterer no longer moistens rebirth with conceptually acquired craving; yet craving seeds are not wholly destroyed, as the treatise's exception says. The English omits 纏 and 發生後有, and "never again" reads as a total end of craving, which only the closing clause qualifies.

quiz.q: Why are these called mind-dissociated? How does the treatise answer?
options: because they arise with mind but oppose it
because they are a real group outside the five aggregates
because they appear only in the two mindless attainments
these are mere conceptual designations made for speech, being neither form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible
quiz.why: The treatise answers that these are mere conceptual designations established within various matters for verbal expression, neither form nor formless, neither visible nor invisible. Master Cháng Bǎi: they are only established through verbal designation, with no substance, and are not really existing phenomena. So the name marks what they are not, not a further entity.

quiz.q: What are the self-characteristic and shared characteristic of form?
options: self-characteristic: six kinds, or the two of bodily and mental feeling; shared: reception
self-characteristic: eleven kinds, or the two of elements and derived form; shared characteristic: mutability and obstruction
self-characteristic: eighteen kinds, or the two of faculty and object; shared characteristic: equal apprehension of the object
self-characteristic: five kinds, or wholesome and unwholesome; shared: active construction
quiz.why: The treatise gives eleven kinds, the ten material sense-bases and form in the sense-base of mental objects; altogether two, the four great elements and derived form; and as the shared mark, mutability and obstruction. Master Cháng Bǎi: because form has these two senses of change and obstruction, the shared nature of the form aggregate is this mark.

quiz.q: How are bodily and mental feeling distinguished, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: feeling based on form and joined with the five is bodily; feeling from the formless mental faculty contacting mental objects is mental
painful feeling is bodily; pleasant feeling is mental; neutral feeling is neither
feeling of the desire realm is bodily; that of the higher realms is mental
defiled feeling is bodily; pure feeling is mental
quiz.why: The treatise says feeling dependent on form is called bodily feeling and feeling dependent on the formless is called mental feeling. Master Cháng Bǎi: feeling arising with form as its basis is bodily feeling, that is, feeling joined with the five consciousnesses; the mental faculty is a formless mental phenomenon, and feeling from its contact with mental objects is mental feeling. Pleasure and pain are a different axis.

quiz.q: The English has "a mental faculty functioning apart from any body" for 意根離身而轉. Is "any" appropriate?
options: "any" is an addition: the lecture says no coarse form aggregate, and the treatise later allows subtle form born of absorption
"any" is right: the formless realm has no form of any sort, even from absorption
"any" is wrong: 離身 means leaving the desire-realm body, a form-realm body remaining
"any" is wrong: the Chinese says the five faculties, not the mental faculty, leave the body, so the subject is mistaken
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of the formless realm have no coarse form aggregate, and the mental faculty can function alone without relying on a physical body. Later in this fascicle the treatise itself says that the formless realm's lack of form refers to form from karma, not to the exceedingly subtle form born of absorption. So the English "any" says more than the Chinese.

quiz.q: Among the six perceptions, what is unmarked perception?
options: perception bound by the desire and form realms
the perception of the summit of existence, with every transmundane perception of those in training and beyond
perception bound by infinite space and infinite consciousness
perception bound by the sphere of nothingness
quiz.why: The treatise defines unmarked perception as the perception of the summit of existence together with every transmundane perception of those in training and beyond. All those before are called marked perception. Master Cháng Bǎi notes of the first part: it is perception of the peak sphere, not yet beyond the three realms, and so still worldly. The word "unmarked" therefore covers worldly and transmundane alike.

quiz.q: By what five kinds do formations cause the mind to act?
options: yielding to the object, uniting with it, separating from it, generating defiled karma, enabling the mind to turn freely
reception, equal apprehension, construction, discernment, and accumulation
object, reception, designation, delusion, and true meaning
object, temporal phase, defilement, purity, and construction
quiz.why: The treatise lists yielding to the object, uniting with it, separating from it, generating defiled karma, and enabling the mind to turn freely. Master Cháng Bǎi: in uniting, this thought hopes to join with the object; enabling the mind to follow wisdom is its turning freely. The third and fourth options are perception's five discriminations and the five aspects of formations' distinctions.

quiz.q: The English has "yielding to the object" for 為境隨與. According to the Sub-commentary and Master Cháng Bǎi, what does 隨與 follow?
options: 隨與 means giving goods to the world, so it should be "giving"
隨與 is craving chasing the object, so "yielding" fits its defiled sense
隨與 is feeling following pain and pleasure, unrelated to perception or volition
as perception receives the object, volition follows along and moves the mind to receive it; this is not submission, so "yielding" is imprecise
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary says that as perception receives the object, this constructing volition accompanies its force. Master Cháng Bǎi: volition then follows along and moves the mind to receive the object; towards the agreeable it wishes to join, from the disagreeable to separate. So 隨與 is a neutral function of joining in, and the English "yielding to the object" suggests giving way or submission.

quiz.q: How are the eighteen self-natures of consciousness counted?
options: six faculties, six objects, and six consciousnesses, the same as the eighteen elements
six consciousnesses in each of the three realms
six consciousnesses each wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral
six consciousnesses, plus three by reception, six by object-apprehension, and three by temporal stage
quiz.why: The treatise first gives six consciousnesses, then three further distinctions: reception threefold, object-apprehension sixfold, and temporal stage threefold. Master Cháng Bǎi: these three add up to twelve, and with the six consciousnesses arising from the six faculties the total is eighteen. These are not the eighteen elements, though the number coincides.

quiz.q: The treatise names a shared characteristic for the other aggregates but none for consciousness. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this?
options: consciousness has no shared characteristic, since the eight differ
consciousness's shared nature is discernment, easy to understand, and so it is left unsaid
its shared characteristic is reception, already given under feeling, and so need not be repeated
a line has dropped out, and equal apprehension should be restored
quiz.why: The treatise concludes the aggregate with the eighteen self-natures alone. Master Cháng Bǎi: the shared nature of consciousness is discernment, which is easy to understand, and so it is left unsaid. The English overview presents the mark of discernment as part of the treatise's summary, but this comes from the lecture.

quiz.q: What does "aggregate" mean, and to reveal what were the aggregates established?
options: the meaning is covering; they were established to reveal a true self
the meaning is growth; they were established to reveal real seeds
the meaning is accumulated gathering; they were established to reveal selflessness
the meaning is distinction; they were established to reveal five separate realities
quiz.why: The treatise gathers each aggregate's kinds, past, future, and present through far and near, and says this accumulated gathering is the meaning of "aggregate." It adds that the aggregates are nothing but variously named conditioned phenomena, established to reveal selflessness. Master Cháng Bǎi: out of compassion for confused beings, the Buddha established the five aggregates so they might realise their selfless nature.
